senses.definition: (golf) A golf shot that curves intentionally to the player's right (if they are right-handed) or to the left (if left-handed).

quotes.text: If you confine yourself to hitting straight shots while you are developing your golf swing, you are less likely to develop a preference for hitting a fade or a draw.
quotes.reference: 2011, James Lythgoe, The Golf Swing: It's all in the hands, page 88:

senses.definition: A haircut where the hair is short or shaved on the sides of the head and longer on top. See also high-top fade and low fade.
(music, cinematography) A gradual decrease in the brightness of a shot or the volume of sound or music (as a means of cutting to a new scene or starting a new song).
(slang) The act of disappearing from a place so as not to be found; covert departure.

quotes.text: Ace could have done a fade. Instead, he gathered all his courage — which was not inconsiderable, even in his middle age — and went to see the Flying Corson Brothers.

senses.definition: (transitive, golf) To hit the ball with the shot called a fade.

quotes.text: The Golden Bear faded the ball from left to right with great consistency, so he seldom had to worry about trouble on the left.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To grow weak; to lose strength; to decay; to perish gradually; to wither, as a plant.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To sink away; to disappear gradually; to grow dim; to vanish.
examples: The milkman's whistling faded into the distance.

1856, Eleanor Marx-Aveling (translator), Gustave Flaubert, Madame Bovary, Part III Chapter XI,
A strange thing was that Bovary, while continually thinking of Emma, was forgetting her. He grew desperate as he felt this image fading from his memory in spite of all efforts to retain it. Yet every night he dreamt of her; it was always the same dream. He drew near her, but when he was about to clasp her she fell into decay in his arms.
